ratings_why.fun: One shared count (times played dead) that every card feeds or reads makes the board easy to grow and fun to watch climb toward Ardea's rave.
ratings_why.distinct: A death that pays out but keeps the body is a fresh twist on Deathrattle and Reborn, and cueing your own deaths gives it a play pattern no current tribe has.

verdict_why: v3 cleared the Tail, Villain and Natrix-with-Old-Crest confusions; what is left is wording polish, and more passes would make it different, not better.

points.text: The Barnstormer's Ham should say "plays dead without dying", like the Understudy and Broken Heart, so no one thinks it drops to 1 Health.
Dame Natrix is the longest card; the Old Crest sentence could move to Old Crest alone, since his text already says ordered steps repeat.
The fantasy lands in what cards do: the critic eats a weak cast, the house snake makes friendly kills safe, the adders really hit each other. Keep that voice in later passes.
Little Anguis still needs its token card to be read; showing the current Tail size right on Anguis's art would make it glanceable.

standouts.why: Mr Ardea Grey: rave or pan on a visible count is clear, funny and exactly the critic who eats actors.
Žaltys turns the household guardian into the rule that makes self-kills safe; flavour and function in one line.
The Barnstormer, a ham who collapses at every scratch, is the clearest read of the tribe's idea at Tier 3.

weakest.why: Dame Natrix is great flavour but too long to read at a glance mid-shop.
Wings Understudy's swap, Attack gain and self play-dead are three steps on one Tier 2 card.
Heap Hatchling is just Play Dead; fine as the plain form, but nothing to read or chase.

flags.note: Blood-and-Thunder with Broken Heart and Old Crest is quadratic damage, held only by the 10-a-throw cap.
Ham doesn't say whether the Barnstormer keeps its Health or drops to 1 when it plays dead.
